title: What is a UTR Number? Full Form, Meaning, Uses & How to Check It
summary: Learn what UTR stands for, how to find your UTR number for NEFT, RTGS or UPI payments, and how to use the reference to track a transfer.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


### TL;DR


UTR stands for Unique Transaction Reference. Use it to trace an NEFT or RTGS transfer. For UPI, look for the 12-digit reference in your app or bank statement. Check the recipient’s bank record to confirm the credit.


A UTR number (Unique Transaction Reference) is a unique identifier for a bank transfer in India. When you make an online payment, you might notice a long string of letters and numbers on your transaction details. This unique code is the UTR number, and it helps your bank check whether the payment has been processed. Most people don’t pay much attention to it until they need to track or verify a payment.


Whether you are a business owner or a freelancer, a UTR is a useful number to see if your transaction was actually processed. It’s more than just banking jargon. It’s key to tracking and verifying the details of a transaction with your bank.


In this guide, you will learn what a UTR number is, its full form, importance, and how to find it easily.


##


**What Does a UTR Number Mean?**


UTR stands for **Unique Transaction Reference** . It is the reference that helps trace your money transfer when you use systems like NEFT or RTGS in India. UPI uses a similar reference. Your bank uses this number to identify a specific transaction. You can think of it as a serial number for your payment, which makes tracing a transaction easier.


You may be wondering why it is called a UTR number. The word “number” is technically redundant here. The full form of UTR, as mentioned before, is Unique Transaction Reference. As its name suggests, the unique reference identifies one transaction within its payment system.


The purpose of a UTR number is accountability. A UTR ensures that there is a concrete record of the transaction in the banking system. It’s also an important tool to help settle disputes, because with a UTR, a bank can check whether the money is still on the way.


##


**Features and Structure of a UTR Number**


### **Format and number of digits**


The format of a particular UTR number depends on the[payment method](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/payment-mode-types/) used. For example, for RTGS transfers, the UTR is a 22-character alphanumeric code, as described in the[RBI’s RTGS FAQs](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/FAQView.aspx?Id=65) . It might look something like` HDFCR52024050921347291` .


It’s important to understand that the full alphanumeric code identifies the transaction. Copy the first few letters and the rest of the number as they appear on your receipt.


For UPI payments, the reference number is a bit shorter, at 12 digits. It is generated in a format like` 123456789102` .


### Example of a UTR Number


Here is a fictional example of a UTR number and its format for better clarity.


` SBINR52023051512345678`


The full reference in this example has 22 characters. This level of detail helps banks trace your transaction.


### How UTR Numbers Are Generated


You don’t need to do anything specific to generate UTR numbers. They are assigned by payment processing systems when you make a transfer.


The IFSC code, date, payment method and transaction amount are useful details when you ask your bank to trace a payment.


Since they are system-generated codes, you can copy the number directly from the transfer details. It is also worth noting that these numbers are non-editable. Once a transaction is processed, use the same UTR in any follow-up with your bank.


##


Why Is a UTR Number Important?


Now that you understand a UTR number and its structure, let’s talk about its importance in the real world.


### Transaction Tracking and Verification


Tracking is one of the main benefits of having a UTR number. Picture this. Your client sends you money for a recent order, but you don’t see that payment in your account. In this case, a UTR number is the reference you need. You can provide this number to the bank, and they can trace the status of your payment. This will help you know whether the payment is pending, completed, or failed.


Doing so also helps you verify that the payment reached the correct account. Check the recipient’s bank statement for the matching credit.


### Dispute Resolution


Things can get messy in matters involving money disputes. The UTR number helps the bank investigate. Both the sender and the receiver can contact their banks and share the UTR number to trace what went wrong. For a merchant payment processed by Cashfree, the[customer query guide](https://www.cashfree.com/customer-query-resolution-guide/) explains which details to share.


Was there a technical failure? Did the money land in the wrong account? Or is there any other reason? Relying on a UTR number, especially in B2B transactions, can really help, as the transaction amount is quite high.


### Significance in Accounting and Taxation


UTR numbers help finance teams[reconcile bank statements](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/reconciling-your-payment/) , validate entries, and match payment records during the audit. In taxation, especially under GST or income tax filings, the UTR can support the evidence for payments made or received.


This is extremely helpful when checking a refund, matching invoices, or supporting documentation during assessments. In[ecommerce payment reconciliation](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/ecommerce-payment-reconciliation/) , teams may also use the settlement UTR to match a payout from the gateway to a bank credit.


### Enhancing Security and Transparency


The UTR number adds a layer of transparency to the process. Since every transfer has a specific ID, you can use that reference to check the credit in your own bank account. UTR numbers can help you verify digital transactions, especially when dealing with new clients or suppliers. A reference shown in a[fake payment screenshot](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/fake-payment-screenshot-scams/) can be fabricated, so check your own bank or merchant record.


##


Types of UTR Numbers Based on Transaction Modes


UTR numbers vary depending on the payment method used. So, when you transfer a large sum via RTGS or split a party bill through UPI, the code generated will be different.


You can find the UTR numbers generated based on different transaction modes below.


### NEFT Transactions


NEFT stands for National Electronic Funds Transfer. This payment method uses a UTR number or transaction reference.[NEFT](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/neft-transfer-time-limits-settlement-process/) is also processed in half-hour batches rather than in real time.


Once your NEFT payment is processed, both the sender and the receiver can ask their banks to use the UTR to track its status.


Remember that this number may also appear on your transaction receipt and SMS/email confirmation.


### RTGS Transactions


RTGS stands for Real Time Gross Settlement. These transactions are quite similar to NEFT transactions. The main difference is in the speed and size of transactions. RTGS transactions are for high-value transfers of ₹2 lakh or more. Furthermore, they are processed individually in real time. This means that when you hit “Send” and the bank submits the transfer to RTGS, the system processes it in real time. For more on the limits, see the[comparison of IMPS, NEFT and RTGS](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/imps-vs-neft-vs-rtgs/) .


An RTGS UTR number has 22 characters. We have already seen its structure at the beginning.


### UPI Transactions


UPI is one of the most used payment methods in India today. You might not have noticed, but UPI transactions generate a reference too. Unlike alphanumeric RTGS codes, the UTR number shown for a UPI payment is a 12-digit Retrieval Reference Number (RRN).


A UPI reference number doesn’t have any letters. It is a number-based code. For example,` 123456789102` could be used to illustrate a UPI reference number.


A UPI ID or[virtual payment address](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/vpa-in-upi/) identifies where to send the payment. The RRN identifies a particular payment.


##


UTR vs UPI Reference Number vs Transaction ID


Many people confuse UTR with a transaction ID. A UTR is a reference used by the bank, whereas a payment gateway can generate a separate transaction ID for its own records.


For instance, when you transfer money via GPay, you get a UPI transaction ID in the app. You can match this transaction reference to the entry in your bank statement using Google Pay’s instructions.


You may see both of these numbers in your transaction history. When you deal with a payment issue, the UTR or RRN helps the bank trace the transfer. The app’s transaction ID might be more helpful if there is a technical glitch and you’re contacting the app or payment gateway.


Reference Where to find it When to use it


NEFT or RTGS UTR Bank statement, transfer receipt or internet banking Ask the bank to trace a bank transfer


UPI reference or RRN UPI transaction details or bank statement Match a UPI payment or raise a dispute


App or gateway payment ID Payment app, merchant dashboard or receipt Help the app or gateway find its payment record


##


How to Check Your UTR Number Online or in an App


So the question is, where exactly do you find this UTR number? Surprisingly, this number is hiding in plain sight, you just need to know where to look.


We have outlined 4 easy ways to find your UTR depending on how you made the payment and which tools you prefer using.


### Method 1. Bank Statement or Passbook


This is an old-school method, but it is still effective. You can check your bank statement if you’ve ever made an NEFT/RTGS or UPI transaction. It doesn’t matter if it’s printed or digital.


For a transfer listed in your bank statement, look for its reference number or UTR. The label can vary by bank.


In some cases, especially with older passbooks, your UTR number may be printed under labels like “Ref No.”, “Txn ID” or simply “UTR”.


### Method 2. Internet Banking


If you use internet banking, finding the UTR number is extremely easy. You just need to log in. Go to your account statement or recent transactions and look for the payment you wish to track.


Then, click or tap for more details, and you easily see the UTR number, especially for any NEFT or RTGS payments.


If you’re checking for UPI transfers, some banks may display it under the “Remarks” or “Narrations” section.


### Method 3. Mobile Banking Apps


All you need to do is open your mobile banking app, navigate to your transaction history or payment section, and find the payment you’re curious about. Once you tap on that transaction, you’ll see a detailed view with the field name “UTR”, “Ref no”, or “Transaction ID”.


As mentioned before, the reference usually consists of 12 digits for UPI. For NEFT and RTGS, copy it exactly as it appears in your bank’s records.


### Method 4. Payment Confirmation, Email or SMS


Once you make a payment, your bank or UPI app usually sends a confirmation email or SMS. These messages often include the UTR number. The only issue with this method is that you must scroll a lot through your email inbox or SMS history to get the exact transaction.


Searching for keywords like “Reference number” or “Transaction ID” may help sort through a huge amount of data.


For a payment made through the[Cashfree UPI payment gateway](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-payment-gateway/) , the merchant can also check the corresponding payment record in its dashboard.


##


Step-by-Step Guide to Check Your UTR Number Online


If you’re more of a DIY person, here’s a simplified process to help you find your UTR number using internet banking without the need to call your bank or wait in long queues.


### Step 1. Log In to Your Bank’s Internet Banking Portal


First of all, you need to go to your bank’s official website and log in using your username and password. At this stage, make sure you’re on the bank’s official site. For this, you can look for the correct website address in the browser bar.


### Step 2. Open Your Transaction History or Account Statement


Once you log in, look for a tab that says “Account summary”, “Transaction history”, or “Statements”, then click on the account where you made the payment.


### Step 3. Locate the Relevant Transaction


This might seem a bit tough, however, you need to scroll thoroughly through the list of recent transactions and find the one you want to track. You can make the process easy by filtering entries based on date, amount, or transaction type.


### Step 4. Copy the UTR Number


After you find the required transaction, click on it to view the full details. You may see a field marked as “UTR number”, “Reference ID” or “Reference No.”. You can copy it and follow up with your bank to track the transaction further.


##


Tracking the Status of a Transaction With a UTR Number


The UTR number is basically your transaction’s tracking number. You can use it to ask your bank to confirm if the money has been credited to the recipient. If you’re dealing with a delayed or[failed transfer](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/why-do-online-payments-fail/) , this number helps the bank or app support trace whether the payment is pending, completed or failed.


### Using Bank Portals and Mobile Apps


Some banks let you enter the UTR directly into a “Track transaction” feature on their website or app. Others may ask you to raise a service request. Alternatively, you can contact customer care and quote the UTR. They’ll check their systems and tell you what’s going on. For UPI, you can use the help option in your UPI app to raise a complaint. Cashfree users can also[check a payment or refund](https://www.cashfree.com/track-payment-status/verify/) using the details requested on the page.


### When and Why to Track a UTR


You usually don’t need to track UTRs unless something goes wrong. But here are a few scenarios where it’s useful:


- The recipient says they haven’t received the money.
- The transaction is marked “Successful” on your end, but the recipient hasn’t received it.
- You need to provide a payment reference for refunds, business invoices or[settlement reconciliation](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/payment-settlement-cycle-explained/) .
- You’re filing a complaint about a[pending payment](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/pending-payment/) or failed transfer.


Basically, if there’s a gap between your money leaving and arriving, your UTR is the breadcrumb trail that helps banks investigate it.


##


Conclusion


UTRs serve a useful purpose. If something goes wrong with a payment, the reference can help your bank find out exactly what happened.


A few easy tips that you can follow:


- Take a screenshot or note down the UTR when you make a payment, especially big ones.
- Keep the UTR nearby if you’re waiting on a refund or need to check if money was sent properly.
- Keep the UTR private. Share it with your bank if they ask for it while solving a problem.


##


FAQs


#### What Is a UTR Number and What Does It Mean?


A UTR (Unique Transaction Reference) number is a unique code banks use to identify and track payments in systems like NEFT and RTGS. UPI has a similar reference called an RRN.


#### What Is the UTR Number Full Form?


The full form of UTR is Unique Transaction Reference.


#### What Is the UTR Number in GPay?


When you send money through Google Pay, you can look up the payment reference in your transaction history. You’ll find it in the transaction details inside the app, usually under “UPI Transaction ID”. It’s a 12-digit number that helps trace payments if anything goes off track.


#### Can a UTR Number Be Used to Resolve a Disputed Transaction?


Yes. If something goes wrong, your UTR number can help. Say the money leaves your account but doesn’t reach the other side, it is the UTR that the bank or support team will use to find the payment in their system. Just share it when you raise a complaint, so the support team can trace it.


#### How Many Digits Are in NEFT, RTGS and UPI Reference Numbers?


UTR numbers vary depending on how you made the payment:


- **UPI.** 12 digits. This is an all-numbers code.
- **NEFT.** Use the UTR or transaction reference shown by your bank. This is often a mix of letters and numbers.
- **RTGS.** 22 characters long. It includes letters and numbers.


Each one is designed to make your transaction trackable in its own system. So, while the size varies, they all do the same job, i.e., help trace your money.


#### What Is the Difference Between a UTR and a Transaction ID?


A UTR is a kind of transaction ID. For example, your wallet app might show a “Transaction ID” that’s only used internally. A UTR is the reference your bank can use when you do an NEFT or RTGS transfer. If you need to talk to customer support about UPI, keep the UPI reference handy so they can check the status of your payment.


#### How to Find the UTR Number for UPI Transactions?


Just open your UPI app like GPay, PhonePe, or Paytm. Go to your transaction history, and tap on the payment. The UTR will usually be labelled something like “UPI Transaction ID” or “Ref No.” It’s a 12-digit number that’s easy to spot. If you’re ever stuck or need to raise an issue, this is one of the numbers you may need.


#### What to Do if You Cannot Find Your UTR Number?


Firstly, don’t panic. You can try checking your bank’s mobile app, internet banking, or even your SMS or email alerts. The UTR is usually in there. If you still can’t find it, you can contact your bank’s customer service with your account number, the amount sent, and the date of the transaction. The customer support team will be able to find the UTR for you. Just make sure you act sooner rather than later, especially if it’s a failed payment.


UTR is a small element on the page, but it can save you a lot of stress. So next time you send money, don’t ignore that number. It might just save the day when things don’t go as planned.
